title: 3D Visualization of Phase Boundaries by Multislice Electron Ptychography
content: Since the first demonstration as a transistor in 2012, Ga2O3 has been extensively investigated as an ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor for its large critical electrical field tolerance in high power device applications. Ga2O3 possesses six known polymorphs (α, β, γ, κ, ε and δ), where the β phase is the thermodynamically stable phase. However, γ-phase inclusions are commonly observed in doped, alloyed or implanted β-Ga2O3 [1]. The γ-phase is thought to be kinetically favored over the more thermodynamically stable β-Ga2O3 when there is disorder resulting in a highly defective local environment. Defects in β-Ga2O3 such as clustered interstitial-divacancy complexes have been calculated by density functional theory (DFT) and have been suggested to resemble the γ-phase when existing in high concentrations [2, 3]. Another theory proposes γ-phase and β-phase share a common sublattice of oxygen which allows the diffusion of Ga interstitials to enable phase transformation [4].
